title: Don't Get Heartbroken: AG Announces Tools to Prevent, Report Romance Scams
body_html:
If you or someone you know may be a target, call 1-855-961-7226.
In a news release, the Ohio Attorney General's office announced a new initiative to help Ohioans protect themselves from
romance scams
and get help if they are targeted.
From the release:
Romance scammers, who often prey on older adults, establish a fake online relationship with their victims to gain their trust before requesting money. Such scams often leave victims financially devastated and emotionally isolated, and many cases go unreported because victims feel embarrassed and are thus reluctant to seek help. 
...
The initiative establishes a dedicated hotline – 
1-855-961-SCAM
 – for those who have been victimized or who believe a loved one may be the victim of a romance scam.
For more information, 
read the full release
.

title: Add Your Ohio ID to Google Wallet
body_html:
Virtual IDs are now available for citizens with Apple or Android devices.
In a news release, the Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles announced that Ohioans can now add their Ohio Driver License or State ID to
Google Wallet
. 
From the release:
Ohio Mobile ID in Google Wallet allows users to securely store and present their identity information. When an ID is displayed, the user can review exactly what data is shared. Digital IDs are encrypted on the device and protected by personal authentication. If a device is lost or stolen, digital IDs can be deleted through remote data erase features.
Ohio Mobile ID
is now available on both Apple and Android devices.
For more information, 
read the full release
.

title: Summer Hotel Health and Safety Tips from the State Fire Marshal
body_html:
Regular inspections, simple steps help keep vacationers safe in Ohio.
In a news release, the Ohio Department of Commerce Division of State Fire Marshal highlights the work they do to keep vacationers safe in Ohio's
hotels and motels
. They also offer consumer tips to ensure a safe, healthy, and enjoyable stay.
From the release:
“Summer is the time of year to unplug, enjoy some well‑deserved vacation, and make memories with friends and family,” said State Fire Marshal Kevin Reardon. “Our inspectors are out there every day conducting routine inspections of licensed hotels to ensure they are safe, clean, and in compliance with state building and fire codes. We want every hotel guest to feel confident when they check in for their stay.”
Examples of fire safety-related items inspectors look for include missing annual certifications for fire alarms, sprinkler systems, and fire extinguishers, while sanitation issues include items such as suspected mold or mildew, stained mattresses or carpets, and bedbugs. In the event a violation is found, inspectors conduct follow-up visits to ensure any discovered issues are resolved prior to the arrival of guests.
Among their tips: Check reviews before booking and inspect the room before paying.
For more tips and information,
read the full release
.

title: September is Ohio Preparedness Month
body_html:
Be ready for all types of emergencies with tips and resources all month long.
The Ohio Emergency Management Agency marks September as
Ohio Preparedness Month
. Visit their website and follow them on social media for themed tips and resources all month long. 
From the release:
“The goal of Ohio Preparedness Month is to encourage families across our state to stay informed, stay connected, and take simple steps that can help them be prepared for emergencies,” said Ohio EMA Executive Director Sima Merick. “Building awareness within your household is one of the most effective ways to keep your loved ones safe.”
For more information, visit the
Ohio Preparedness Month
webpage.

title: 2026 Ohio School Report Cards Show Students are Gaining in Literacy
body_html:
Literacy achievement is at a 5-year high following the implementation of Science of Reading.
In a news release, Governor Mike DeWine, Lt. Governor Jim Tressel, and the Ohio Department of Education announced the release of the
2026 Ohio School Report Cards
, noting improvements in literacy, math, and career readiness.
The results show Ohio students are making significant gains in literacy, with statewide English language arts proficiency reaching a five-year high of 62.2%.
The results also show statewide math proficiency reached a five-year high, while attendance continues to improve and more Ohio students are demonstrating readiness for college, careers, the workforce, and military service.

title: September 25 is Dolly Parton Day in Ohio
body_html:
Dolly Parton Day honors the late country icon's devotion to childhood literacy.
Ohio Governor Mike DeWine has proclaimed Sept. 25, 2026, as 
Dolly Parton Day
to celebrate the "life, legacy, and generosity" of the late country superstar. 
Dolly has a deep connection with Ohio through
Dolly Parton's Imagination Library
, which provides a free book in the mail each month for children under age 5.

title: Reminder: Use Your Food Assistance Benefits at Participating Farmers' Markets
source: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services
body_html:
Look for signs saying that SNAP, EBT, or Direction Card are accepted.
In a news release, the Ohio Department of Job and Family Services announced that residents who receive
food assistance
(also called SNAP) can use their benefits at
participating farmers' markets
across the state.
From the release:
With farmers’ market season in full swing, ODJFS encourages eligible Ohioans to take advantage of this benefit. Participating markets display signs indicating they accept SNAP, EBT, or the Ohio Direction Card. In most cases, cardholders use their Ohio Direction Card to purchase tokens at the market, which can then be used to buy eligible food items.
For more information,
read the full release

title: Team Tressel Fitness Challenge Helps Students Build Healthy Habits
body_html:
A record 650,000 students at 2,100 schools will participate this fall.
In a news release, the Lt. Governor's Office announced record participation in the
Team Tressel Fitness Challenge
by Ohio's schools and students this fall.. 
From the release:
What started just one year ago as a challenge to help Ohio students build healthier habits has quickly grown into a statewide movement. Since its launch in August 2025, student participation has increased by nearly 255%, making the Team Tressel Fitness Challenge one of the largest statewide youth wellness efforts in the country.
But for Tressel, the numbers are only part of the story.
"The most exciting part isn’t how big this Challenge has become. It’s knowing that well over half a million young people are going to learn something about themselves along the way," said Lt. Governor Tressel. "We want every student to discover that when they set a goal, build good habits, and give their best effort every day, there’s no limit to what they can accomplish."
For more information,
read the full release
.

title: Tips to Help Kids go Back to School Healthy and Ready to Learn
body_html:
The Ohio Department of Health has resources for parents from K-12 and beyond.
In a feature story, the Ohio Department of Health has tips to help parents send their children
back to school
healthy and prepared.
From the story:
“A new school year brings fresh opportunities for students to thrive,” said Dr. Mary DiOrio, medical director at the Ohio Department of Health (ODH). “It is important to prepare them for the year ahead by prioritizing their health.” 
Tips cover topics including vaccinations, good sleep habits, healthy lunches, safe transportation, mental health, and more.

title: Buy Ohio-Grown Trees Online from the Buckeye Nursery
body_html:
New online ordering system supports conservation efforts statewide.
In a news release, the Ohio Department of Natural Resources announced that Ohioans can now purchase trees from the
Buckeye State Tree Nursery
online.
Customers can visit
nursery.ohiodnr.gov
to browse available tree species and place orders directly online. The new system expands access to seedlings grown at the Buckeye State Tree Nursery in Zanesville. It allows customers to choose between picking up their orders at the nursery or having seedlings shipped directly to them.

read the full release
.

title: Get Ready for Ohio's Fall Hunting Seasons
body_html:
Check current regulations for changes to season dates and daily limits.
In a news release, the Ohio Department of Natural Resources announced that
Ohio's fall hunting seasons
kick off with squirrel and dove seasons starting September 1. 
From the release:
As the 2026 fall seasons begin, hunters are reminded to check the current regulations for changes to season dates and daily limits. New waterfowl hunting zones take effect this year, so hunters should confirm the zone of their hunting location before the regular seasons kick off in October. A summary of the 
2026-27 hunting and trapping regulations
can be found at wildohio.gov, on the HuntFish OH app, or printed copies where licenses are sold. 
For more information,
read the full release
.

title: On the Bus or in the Car, Make Sure Kids Make it There Safely
body_html:
The Ohio Traffic Safety Office has reminders about sharing the road with buses and tips for safety in the family car.
In a news release, the Ohio Traffic Safety Office highlights two timely
school transportation safety
campaigns, whether you take your child to school in the family car or you are sharing the road with school buses.
From the release:
With students across Ohio returning to classrooms, the Ohio Traffic Safety Office (OTSO), a division of the Ohio Department of Public Safety, is urging all drivers to make safety their top priority during back-to-school season. OTSO is highlighting two statewide education efforts: the Stop Means Stop school bus safety campaign and Buckle Up with Brutus, Ohio’s child passenger safety program for elementary-aged students.

title: Check out the 2026 Ohio Fall Events Guide
body_html:
TourismOhio highlights 440 things to do as the seasons change.
In a news release, TourismOhio announced its
2026 Ohio Fall Events Guide
. 
Now live at Ohio.org, the guide spotlights five standout events from each of Ohio’s 88 counties, making it the ultimate planner for everything from big-time festivals to small-town favorites. Organized by month and region, it's designed to help travelers easily map out cozy date nights, family road trips, and spontaneous getaways all season long.
